violation_type.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children (26 TAC §744.1203(4))
violation_type.short_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children
violation_type.typical_finding: It was found children were leaving the classroom to use the restroom and use the water foutain unsupervised.

finding_variants.text: It was found children were leaving the classroom to use the restroom and use the water foutain unsupervised.
It was found during the course of the investigation that children were not supervised at all times as required while in care at the operation.
Based on the inspection, and interviews, it was found children were not properly supervised on the playground.  A child was injured and the caregiver was unaware.

This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.  A child with a history of wandering and diagnosed special needs, was not appropriately supervised which allowed the child to leave the cafeteria without caregiver knowledge.
During the inspection children were seen leaving the room without notifying a caregiver.
It was found during the investigation a caregiver left a child on the playground unsupervised.

occurrences.finding: Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Based on the preponderance of evidence gathered, there is sufficient evidence to determine deficiencies related to this investigation regarding caregiver responsibilities.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Based on information gathered through the course of the DFPS investigation, it was determined that appropriate and consistent care was not provided for a child with special needs.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Through out the inspection one of the caregivers struggled to maintain control of the children.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Appropriate care was not provided to a child that was known to elope by caregivers. There was not a process in place to address and help prevent the child from exiting the area.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Child unable to take care of own toileting needs was unassisted for over 20 minutes while yelling for assistance.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: This standard was found deficient as part of a DFPS Investigation.  A child with a history of wandering and diagnosed special needs, was not appropriately supervised which allowed the child to leave the cafeteria without caregiver knowledge.

Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance. The caregiver did not have knowledge of the child's ongoing activities. A child received an injury while in care; the child and two other children stated that the child was favoring their arm after the incident.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Two children were not supervised while in the art room.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Two students were left unattended in the gym while the group played outside.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Children were observed going to the bathroom alone.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Chilldren were observed playing on a side of the cafeteria where children couldn't be seen.  Children were also observed standiing at the door after walking from the playground to the door.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Supervision of a child was not maintained when a child was alone on the playground.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: On  two separate occasions during the inspection, I observed children being left alone in the gym while the caregiver left to answer the door.    I also observed children entering the gym from the playground ahead of the caregiver. The second caregiver was not in the gym. She was answering the door.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Three children were unattended in the cafetorium.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Children were observed walking to the front to meet the site director, two children walked into the cafeteria area without any caregivers before the site director walked in an walked them to the door to meet their parents.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: The children were not being supervised properly.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child was able to leave the operation unsupervised.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child ran out of the cafetorium twice into an unlicensed space where the caregiver was unable to locate the child for several minutes.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A caregiver did not properly supervise a child when allowing the child to go down the hallway to the restroom alone.  This occurred during a transition time where the hallway was filled with people not associated with the program which prevented the caregivers from having visual and auditory awareness, physical proximity to the child, and the ability to have knowledge of the child's activities.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: It was observed that 48 children in care were not being adequately supervised by two caregivers.  Children were observed hiding out of sight, running in unsupervised hallways, plugging in cell phone chargers, using personal cell phones without content supervision and crawling into an unsupervised kitchen area.  Caregivers were asked to regain control before licensing left the operation.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: At arrival, I observed a child left alone sleeping at a table in the cafeteria for approximately 2 minutes.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Two children in care were observed walking out of the cafeteria and to the playground unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: This standard was evaluated in regard to an investigation and a violation was found. The operation staff encouraged the child to re-join the group but the child left the premise of the operation. Although the staff saw the child left the premise and the staff continued following the child, the staff lost the supervision of the child. The operation called the police right away, the staff kept looking for the child and the child was later found by the police.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Caregiver allowed a child to leave the cafeteria unsupervised and child was found 6 minutes later at the front of the ISD building.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on the information received during the investigation there is a violation of this standard.  A child walked out of the operation and was found outside by a school faculty member.  The caregivers didn't know that the child had walked out of the operation until the child was brought back inside of the building by a school faculty member.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Children were allowed to use boxcutters with no adult supervision.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Children were observed in the restroom unsupervised.     Children were observed not being supervised in the cafeteria. Children were running around and playing on cafeteria tables.     Caregivers were walking around not redirecting children.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: At the time of the inspection, there was a child left in a classroom, away from the other groups, for around 6 minutes.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During the inspection two different caregivers were observed leaving two different groups of children in the cafeteria while they left the building to speak with parents parked outside of the building.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on information obtained during the investigation, it was determined that two children were able to engage in inappropriate behavior due to a lack of supervision.  The caregiver in charge was not aware of the children's ongoing activities and did not have visual and/or auditory awareness of the children.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on the information obtained the caregivers were not properly supervising the children in care.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: One child was left in the gym alone.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: At the time of the inspection children were observed going through two sets of doorways and the length of the cafeteria to use the restroom without a caregiver supervising them, or their designated caregiver notifying another caregiver the children were going through the are to the restroom to have them supervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on information obtained through an investigation it was found that a caregiver did not supervise children adequately when one was dismissed from care without a parent being present and a second child left the facility with their parent without the caregiver knowing.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: It was found during the investigation a caregiver left a child on the playground unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: This standard was part of an investigation.  It was determined a caregiver was not appropriately supervising some of the children.  The caregiver was not aware of the activities of the children when they were jumping off the bleachers.  This resulted in a child breaking their leg.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Two caregivers were unaware that a child was alone in the cafeteria.  One caregiver did not know how many children they were supervising.  One child was observed walking to the restroom unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: The site director left children alone and unsupervised in the gynasimum when they exited the gym to answer the door. One caregiver was not aware that a child was about leave the area unescorted.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child had an accident while in care, caregiver unable to provide details of the accident.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Two children were observed leaving the gym unsipervised.  One of the children was observed trying to open an exit door.  The site director who was supervising the children was made aware by Licensing staff that the children were in the hallway unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: On three separate occasions during the inspection, I observed a child chase a ball out of the cafeteria and down a hallway. The caregivers who were engaged in a table activity with the rest of the children did not see the child leave the cafeteria.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During the course of investigation, it was determined that a child left the building and was unsupervised.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During the follow-up inspection the children in care were observed to be in a room without any adult supervision for approximately 1 minute. Caregiver was down the hall from the children taking a child to their parent.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During transition from the playground, children who were going home were left without adult supervision in the gymnasium when the escorting caregiver walked them to the door leading into the gymnasium and then closed the door without the caregiver who was receiving the children being in the gymnasium.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Younger children were able to walk down the hallway to the restrooms alone, they was not a caregiver supervising the child as they walk down the hallway to the restroom or back to the classroom. Children were allowed to walk around to the dismissal area with out an caregiver.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child was unattended outside while waiting on their parent to pull up. Other children were able to walk around the halls to the restroom, and to the front area to live for the day with out a caregiver

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on the information obtained during the investigation, it was determined staff did not supervise children when a child in care walked out the gym unsupervised.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: It was found children were leaving the classroom to use the restroom and use the water foutain unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: At the time of the inspection, children were not being monitored appropriately. There were children walking the hallways and transitioning between rooms alone.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Caregiver took a child to the restroom and left 8 children alone in the cafeteria unsupervised.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A caregiver left five children unsupervised in the cafeteria to walk a child/ren down the hallway so they could be picked up by their parent. The caregiver was observed at the front door to release children to their parents upon arrival to the inspection.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child was left unsupervised on a field trip for up to 10 minutes.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: It was found during the investigation that two children were able to leave the cafeteria and go into the gym for an unknown amount of time.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During the follow-up inspection to evaluate supervision of children, school-age children were observed entering the gymnasium without caregivers present. The children were in the gym for approximately 5 minutes before a caregiver came into the building.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: This standard was evaluated in regard to an investigation and found to be in violation of minimum standards.  The caregiver did not conduct a name to face recognition prior to transitioning to another area.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Four caregivers did not know many children they were supervising in a large group.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: During this inspection I observed two children ages 11 and 12 years old alone in a classroom.     During this inspection I observed a group of seven children unsupervised in the gym.     During this inspection I observed a 9 year old alone in a classroom.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Interviews were conducted and procedures were evaluated. It was determined that school-age children were unsupervised in the restroom.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A child was left unttended in the hallway. The caregivers did not have visual or auditory awareness of the child.
Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: An 11 year old child was able to leave the operation without a caregiver knowing where they went.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A caregiver left their group of children unsupervised in a classroom. The caregiver left the group to open the front door for the inspector.     The same caregiver was observed leaving their group of children unsupervised again later during the inspection.

Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: Based on the information gathered, a caregiver left a child on the playground unsupervised for approximately 2-3 minutes. The child was found safe and returned to the after-school program by a parent.
